comparison: Both strongly support the experimental design and atlas generation methodology (C8, C38, C42-C48, C67-C70). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers describe the approach as 'ingenious' and an 'invaluable resource.' High agreement on methodology quality.
Perfect alignment on mixed lineage composition findings (C50-C52). Both accept the observation and the authors' acknowledgment of alternative explanations. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Both address TF expression patterns (C112-C124). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with caveat that combinatorial code requires functional validation. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting the mechanistic conclusions are correlational and need experimental validation. Agreement on descriptive data, divergence on confidence level for interpretive claims.

Both support neurotransmitter characterization (C76-C85). OpenEval finds data convincing with clear quantitative support. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of study strengths without concerns. Strong agreement.

Both support neuron-to-cluster mapping (C14, C15, C39, C125). OpenEval notes multiple complementary approaches strengthen mapping while acknowledging need for validation. Peer reviewers describe methodology as 'validated' and data as 'convincing.' Strong agreement on mapping quality.

Both address neuropeptide mapping (C102-C110). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with strong genetic validation evidence. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting functional implications remain untested and TF-neuropeptide relationships are correlational. Agreement on descriptive findings, divergence on mechanistic interpretation confidence.

Both support glial characterization from T1+T2 atlas (C9, C55-C63). OpenEval provides detailed validation of canonical markers and differential expression analysis. Peer reviewers accept findings without critique as part of study strengths. Strong agreement.

Both support T1 atlas characterization and T1/T2 comparison (C64-C65, C126-C128). OpenEval and peer reviewers accept quantitative cluster identification. Both treat Kenyon cell speculation appropriately as reasonable interpretation rather than definitive conclusion. Strong agreement.

Both support T2 neuronal atlas composition (C11, C74-C75). OpenEval validates quantitative data and transcriptional uniqueness claims. Peer reviewers accept cluster numbers and characterization as 'convincing.' Strong agreement.

Both address sex differences in T2 glia (C91-C96). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with clear documentation. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN, noting the observation is 'striking' but functional significance is not tested or discussed extensively. Agreement on data quality, divergence on interpretation completeness.

Both address sex differences in T2 neurons (C97-C101). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, paralleling glial findings. Peer review marks as UNCERTAIN with same concern about untested functional significance. Agreement on descriptive findings, divergence on interpretation adequacy.

Both support T2 glial atlas characterization (C86-C90). OpenEval validates quantitative data and cell type identification. Peer reviewers accept glial characterization without concerns. Strong agreement.

Both support forward-looking claims about resource utility (C40, C133). OpenEval marks speculative statements as appropriately framed. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse resource value as 'invaluable' for future studies. Strong agreement on dataset utility.

Both address TF-neuropeptide correlation analysis (C111). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about validation needs. Peer review marks broader neuropeptide/TF claims as UNCERTAIN, noting correlational nature requires functional testing. Subtle divergence in confidence level.

Both address broad interpretation about cluster-neuron correspondence (C16). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting hypothesis requires validation. Peer reviewers support the mapping work overall (SUPPORTED) but within context of validated methodology. Slight divergence in how interpretive claim is weighted.
OpenEval supports T2-enriched marker identification (C53-C54) with clear evidence from Figure 1D. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific marker claims.

OpenEval supports extensive background and context claims (C1-C7, C17-C37, C41, C71-C72, C129-C130, C132, C135, C138) as appropriately referenced. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate background/context claims.

OpenEval supports miscellaneous findings (C10, C66, C73, C134) including sex-enriched clusters, coverage calculations, and glial similarity conclusions. These specific claims not separately evaluated in peer review, though overlapping content addressed in other peer results.
